results.name: game_engine_rasterize_in_game_score
results.evidence: Matches the cea-pdb hint via the '%s (%s)' string; builds tab-separated scoreboard rows (name/service-tag/ping columns, header string 'Ping', row formats '\t%s...' and '*\t%s...') using select_players_to_display, tag_lookup("ui\\multiplayer_game_text"), and renders them with chimera__draw_16_bit_text; also formats and draws the server address via inet_ntoa.
results.summary: Renders the in-game/post-game multiplayer scoreboard (per-player rows with ping, plus the server's IP:port) using the ui\multiplayer_game_text UI tag and chimera__draw_16_bit_text.

results.name: player_team_score_is_positive
results.evidence: Looks up the player's team index from the players array (DAT_0087a480, stride 0x200, +2), then tests a per-team float table (DAT_0087aa14) for >0.0, returning the inverse as a boolean-like predicate; only active when the game engine is running (DAT_006f1d20 != 0).
results.summary: Given a player identifier in EAX, returns whether that player's team currently has a non-positive score (used as a UI/logic predicate).

results.name: unit_current_weapon_prevents_camo_depower
results.evidence: Follows player->unit (players array +0x34) into the object table, reads the unit's current-weapon index (+0x2f2) and weapon object handle (+0x2f8 array), then tests bit 13 of the weapon tag's WeaponFlags field at Item+0x308 (types/tags.h: WeaponFlags bit 13 = does_not_depower_active_camo_in_multilplayer).
results.summary: Returns whether the player's currently-held weapon has the 'does not depower active camouflage in multiplayer' flag set.

results.name: unit_update_active_camouflage_timer
results.evidence: Calls FUN_00466390 (weapon camo-depower flag test) to pick a decay amount, then decrements a per-unit float field at offset 0x37c each call, clamping it to a 0.05 floor and setting a dirty bit at +0x422; only runs while the field is >= 0.05.
results.summary: Decays a unit's active-camouflage-related timer field each tick, using the current weapon's camo-depower flag to determine how fast it counts down.

results.name: game_time_format_minutes_seconds
results.evidence: Divides an ECX-supplied tick count by 30 (ticks->seconds) then splits into minutes (/60) and seconds (%60), formats each half via FUN_00557910, and combines them with the literal format string L"%s:%s".
results.summary: Formats a tick-count time value (register argument) as a "minutes:seconds" wide string.

results.name: ctf_flag_object_clear_carrier
results.evidence: For a given player's unit object, clears flag bit 0x20 at +0x22c, sets +0x204 to the current game time (DAT_006f1d6c+0xc), and resets +0x200 to -1; these exact offsets (+0x200/+0x204/+0x22c bit0x20) are later tested in FUN_00468bf0's auto-return timer logic (elapsed = now - obj+0x204).
results.summary: Resets an objective (flag) game object's carrier/drop-time tracking fields, used when the flag is returned or reset.

results.name: game_variant_sanitize_options
results.evidence: Clamps a series of numeric fields in a struct pointed to by ECX to sane ranges (e.g. +0x30 clamped 1..5, +0x54 float clamped 0.25..4.0, +0x5c clamped 0..13, +0x60 low nibble clamped <=8) and coerces several byte fields to strict booleans -- the shape and offsets match the ~0x98-byte game-variant options struct built by the game_engine_variant_defaults_* functions.
results.summary: Clamps/sanitizes the numeric and boolean fields of a game-variant options struct (passed in ECX) to valid ranges.

results.name: game_engine_resolve_equipment_tag_dependencies
results.evidence: Switches on DAT_006f1ce8 & 0xf; in most cases walks six TagDependency-sized (stride 0x10) fields at object+0x24 and, for each non -1 dependency, calls FUN_004449f0 (a tag-dependency resolver); afterwards does the same over sixteen TagDependency-sized entries at object+0x150, plus two extra checks gated on DAT_006f1cb8==3/1.
results.summary: Resolves a set of tag dependencies (a 6-entry and a 16-entry TagDependency array) inside a map-globals-like structure, selected by a difficulty/type index.

results.name: game_engine_is_valid_spawn_candidate
results.evidence: Returns false when the game engine is active and either flag bit1 of DAT_0087aa00 is set or DAT_0068944c < 1; otherwise, when DAT_0068944c < 2, resolves param_1 via FUN_00474db0 and checks that the resulting player's team field (players array +2) is not -1 (i.e. not an observer).
results.summary: Predicate checking whether a given identifier refers to a usable, team-assigned player under current game-engine constraints.

results.name: unit_current_weapon_must_be_readied_in_ctf
results.evidence: Requires the game engine active and DAT_006f1cb8==1 (matches the classic_ctf variant-defaults local_70 value of 1, from out/phase2/results/game_02.json's decoded default builders), then tests bit 3 (must_be_readied) of the current object's WeaponFlags field at +0x308 via the players/objects array chain.
results.summary: Returns whether the current weapon has the must-be-readied flag while the active game-variant type equals the CTF value (1).

results.name: player_profile_cache_initialize
results.evidence: Guarded by a one-shot flag (DAT_006f1d38); zero-fills the 16-entry, 0x30-byte-stride table at DAT_006b0b88..0x6b0e88 and resets the active-entry count DAT_006f1d34, matching the table layout walked by FUN_00466c60/e80/ee0/00466d00.
results.summary: One-time initializer that clears the 16-slot player-profile cache table used elsewhere in this file.

results.name: player_profile_cache_register_player
results.evidence: Skips registration if FUN_00466e80 already finds a matching entry; otherwise scans the same 16x0x30 table for the first free slot (flag byte ==0), stores the passed-in handle (in_EAX) there, marks it active, and increments DAT_006f1d34.
results.summary: Adds a player handle to the profile-cache table in the first free slot, unless it is already present.

results.name: player_profile_cache_flush_all
results.evidence: Walks all 16 entries of the DAT_006b0b88 profile-cache table calling FUN_00466ee0 on each active one, then invokes an optional engine callback through the vtable-like pointer at DAT_006f1d20+0x90.
results.summary: Processes every active entry in the player-profile cache and then fires an optional game-engine callback.

results.name: player_profile_apply_cached_entry
results.evidence: Locates the caller's slot via FUN_00466e80, then either validates (FUN_004ec590) or updates-and-restores (FUN_004ec600 around a temp copy) the cached profile before copying its fields (offsets 0x9c..0x6c, matching FUN_00466ee0's field list) into a datum_get() result; special-cases DAT_006f1cb8==4 (king-of-the-hill local_70 value) by rescaling a duration field by /30.
results.summary: Applies a cached player-profile entry's fields onto a newly-created datum, with a King-variant-specific time-field rescale.

results.name: game_engine_invoke_optional_engine_callback_94
results.evidence: Trivial wrapper: if the function pointer at DAT_006f1d20+0x94 is non-null, calls it with no arguments -- part of the same vtable-style callback pattern seen at +0x90/+0x58/+0x54/+0xac elsewhere in this file.
results.summary: Invokes the current game-engine's optional callback stored at offset 0x94, if one is registered.

results.name: player_profile_cache_find_slot_by_handle
results.evidence: Walks the 16x0x30 table in groups of 4 unrolled comparisons, matching each entry's active flag and stored value against unaff_ESI, returning the matching slot index (0..15) or -1.
results.summary: Searches the player-profile cache table for an active entry whose stored handle matches the given value, returning its slot index.

results.name: player_profile_cache_capture_player
results.evidence: Given a table slot index, resolves the stored handle via hash_table_get, copies profile-like fields (position/short fields/color-ish dword, offsets 0x9c-0x6c) out of the live players-array entry into a local buffer, rescales a duration field when DAT_006f1cb8==4, forwards the buffer to FUN_00467010, and optionally (param_1==1) writes it back into the cache table.
results.summary: Captures a player's current profile-like fields from the live player record, forwards them for network sync, and optionally refreshes the cache table entry.

results.name: game_engine_send_profile_update_message
results.evidence: Copies the caller's profile buffer onto the stack, calls FUN_004ec940(...,0x15,...) (a message-type-tagged send/validate primitive used the same way at 0x4671d0/0x17 and 0x4682c0/0x16), and on success dispatches via FUN_004e1a80/FUN_004e1930 into the shared network-message-queue global DAT_00871de0.
results.summary: Packages a player-profile buffer as network message type 0x15 and enqueues it for sending/delivery.

results.name: game_engine_countdown_message_stage1
results.evidence: Sets DAT_0087aa10 = 1 and a paired float DAT_0087aa08 = 7.0, then calls FUN_0046be40(0) and FUN_00498650(); reached only from FUN_00467230's in_ECX==1 branch.
results.summary: First stage of a countdown/notification sequence: sets state 1 with a 7-second timer and triggers an update/sound callback.

results.name: game_engine_countdown_message_stage2
results.evidence: Sets DAT_0087aa10 = 2 and DAT_0087aa08 = 5.0, then iterates every player via data_iterator_next clearing bit 0x20 of the corresponding unit's byte field at +0x106; reached from FUN_00467230's in_ECX==2 branch.
results.summary: Second stage of the countdown sequence: sets state 2 with a 5-second timer and clears a per-unit flag for all players.

results.name: game_engine_countdown_message_stage3
results.evidence: Sets DAT_0087aa10 = 3, then either zeroes DAT_0087aa18/DAT_0087aa1c (when DAT_006f1d25=='\x01') or, if DAT_006f1d28 > 0, sets DAT_0087aa18=1 and DAT_0087aa1c to that value; reached from FUN_00467230's in_ECX==3 branch.
results.summary: Third stage of the countdown sequence: sets state 3 and configures a follow-on duration from global settings.

results.name: game_engine_send_network_message_0x16
results.evidence: Builds a tiny fixed payload and calls FUN_004ec940(0,0x16,0,&local_8,0,1,0); on success (>0) forwards it via FUN_004e1a80(1,&DAT_00871de0,1,0,0,3), mirroring the send pattern in FUN_00467010/FUN_004682c0 with a different message-type constant.
results.summary: Sends a small fixed-payload network message tagged with type 0x16.

results.name: game_engine_countdown_message_dispatch
results.evidence: Validates an incoming message via FUN_004ec590 (falls back to FUN_004ec670 on failure) and then dispatches on in_ECX to FUN_004670c0 (1), FUN_004670f0 (2), or FUN_00467180 (3), the three countdown-stage handlers.
results.summary: Validates and dispatches an incoming countdown/notification message to one of its three stage handlers.

results.name: game_engine_variant_defaults_assault
results.evidence: Reached as the terminal fallback of game_engine_get_variant_by_name (0x4622d0) when __stricmp(in_ECX,"assault") == 0; fills a fixed 0x98-byte (0x26-dword) game-variant options buffer identically in shape to the sibling classic_* default builders in game_02.json.
results.summary: Fills a game-variant options buffer with the hardcoded default settings for the built-in "assault" multiplayer game type.

results.name: game_engine_variant_defaults_crazy_king
results.evidence: Directly reached from game_engine_get_variant_by_name's __stricmp(in_ECX,"crazy_king") branch, which calls this exact function to fill the caller's buffer; identical 0x26-dword fixed-write shape to the classic_* builders.
results.summary: Fills a game-variant options buffer with the hardcoded default settings for the built-in "crazy_king" multiplayer game type.

results.name: game_engine_variant_defaults_stalker
results.evidence: Reached from game_engine_get_variant_by_name via a __stricmp against a string that Ghidra shows only as an overlapping pointer into an unrelated symbol (PTR_s_g_objects_equipment_00667450+0x13), so the literal text could not be confirmed directly; positionally it sits between the 'juggernaut' and 'crazy_king' branches, mirroring the classic_juggernaut/classic_stalker/classic_crazy_king ordering in game_02.json, which is the basis for the 'stalker' guess.
results.summary: Fills a game-variant options buffer with hardcoded default settings for a built-in variant reached between the 'juggernaut' and 'crazy_king' name checks (name inferred as "stalker" by analogy, not directly confirmed).

results.name: game_engine_variant_defaults_juggernaut
results.evidence: Directly reached from game_engine_get_variant_by_name's __stricmp(in_ECX,"juggernaut") branch, which calls this exact function to fill the caller's buffer.
results.summary: Fills a game-variant options buffer with the hardcoded default settings for the built-in "juggernaut" multiplayer game type.

results.name: game_engine_variant_defaults_king
results.evidence: Directly reached from game_engine_get_variant_by_name's __stricmp(in_ECX,"king") branch (a string that is pooled as a suffix of "classic_king" and so isn't separately listed in the strings table).
results.summary: Fills a game-variant options buffer with the hardcoded default settings for the built-in "king" (King of the Hill) multiplayer game type.

results.evidence: Directly reached from game_engine_get_variant_by_name's __stricmp(in_ECX,"oddball") branch, which calls this exact function to fill the caller's buffer.
results.summary: Fills a game-variant options buffer with the hardcoded default settings for the built-in "oddball" multiplayer game type.

results.evidence: Directly reached from game_engine_get_variant_by_name's __stricmp(in_ECX,"race") branch (pooled as a suffix of "classic_race", hence not separately listed in the strings table).
results.summary: Fills a game-variant options buffer with the hardcoded default settings for the built-in "race" multiplayer game type.

results.summary: Fills a game-variant options buffer with the hardcoded default settings for the built-in "slayer" multiplayer game type.

results.evidence: Directly reached from game_engine_get_variant_by_name's __stricmp(in_ECX,"team_king") branch, which calls this exact function to fill the caller's buffer.
results.summary: Fills a game-variant options buffer with the hardcoded default settings for the built-in "team_king" multiplayer game type.

results.evidence: Directly reached from game_engine_get_variant_by_name's __stricmp(in_ECX,"team_oddball") branch, which calls this exact function to fill the caller's buffer.
results.summary: Fills a game-variant options buffer with the hardcoded default settings for the built-in "team_oddball" multiplayer game type.

results.evidence: Directly reached from game_engine_get_variant_by_name's __stricmp(in_ECX,"team_race") branch, which calls this exact function to fill the caller's buffer.
results.summary: Fills a game-variant options buffer with the hardcoded default settings for the built-in "team_race" multiplayer game type.

results.evidence: Directly reached from game_engine_get_variant_by_name's __stricmp(in_ECX,"team_slayer") branch, which calls this exact function to fill the caller's buffer.
results.summary: Fills a game-variant options buffer with the hardcoded default settings for the built-in "team_slayer" multiplayer game type.

results.name: game_engine_clear_all_player_unit_flags
results.evidence: Iterates every player via data_iterator_next, and for those with a valid unit handle (+0x34 != -1), clears two byte flags at unit offsets 0x31e and 0x31f (799) in the object table.
results.summary: Clears two per-unit flag bytes for every player's current unit, likely as part of a new-round/new-life reset pass.

results.name: game_engine_objective_reset_and_cleanup_objects
results.evidence: When DAT_00719720==2 (multiplayer game active), zeroes a lifetime-ish field (+0x2c) on every entry from a second data_iterator, clamping a related duration global to a minimum of 0x5a; unconditionally afterwards, walks every object via object_iterator_next deleting/regenerating garbage (object type 0 or 3) via FUN_004f5aa0/FUN_004f59d0.
results.summary: In multiplayer, resets a per-entry duration field across a data table and then sweeps all game objects, deleting stray biped/weapon-type garbage.

results.name: game_engine_cleanup_dead_objects
results.evidence: Walks every game object via object_iterator_next and, for any whose type field (+4) is 0 or 3, calls FUN_004f5aa0 followed by FUN_004f59d0(handle,0) -- the same delete/garbage pattern used in the sibling cleanup functions in this file.
results.summary: Sweeps all live game objects and deletes/garbage-collects any of a specific type (biped or weapon-class, per the +4 type field).

results.name: game_engine_cleanup_orphaned_pickup_objects
results.evidence: Walks every game object; for each, if (DAT_00719720 != 1) or the object's type field is 3, and it isn't a valid, tag-flag-permitted (bit 2 of tag flags) unit-owned parent, it is treated as orphaned and deleted via FUN_004f5aa0/FUN_004f59d0, unless a byte flag (+0x7d bit 0x41) marks it exempt.
results.summary: Sweeps game objects and deletes weapon/pickup-type objects that are no longer validly parented, except when engine type 1 (CTF) applies special handling.

results.name: player_profile_cache_clear_player_stats_block
results.evidence: Walks the 16-entry profile-cache table (DAT_006b0b88, stride 0x30) and, for each active entry, zeroes a 0x3c-byte (0xf dword) block at players-array offset +0x90 for that player's index.
results.summary: Zeroes a per-player statistics/state block for every player currently registered in the profile cache.

results.name: game_engine_cleanup_or_reset_objects
results.evidence: When DAT_006f1cb8==5 (matches the classic_race local_70 value of 5), iterates all objects deleting type-0/3 garbage exactly like FUN_004681a0's siblings; otherwise iterates all objects calling FUN_00570de0 on each -- a different, race-specific-vs-general split.
results.summary: Performs the standard object-cleanup sweep when the active variant type equals the Race value (5), otherwise runs a different per-object handler over all objects.

results.name: game_engine_initialize_new_round
results.evidence: Runs the full reset sequence used elsewhere in this file in order: FUN_00467de0 (clear unit flags), FUN_00467e60 and FUN_00468010/FUN_00467f70 (object cleanup), an optional engine callback at +0xac, sets DAT_0087aa20 from the current game time, calls the already-named game_engine_update_netgame_equipment(1), FUN_004681a0, and FUN_00468150 (clear profile stats block).
results.summary: Runs the game engine's per-round reset sequence: clears unit flags, garbage-collects stray objects, reloads netgame equipment, and clears cached player stats.

results.name: game_engine_send_network_message_0x17
results.evidence: Builds a one-byte payload and calls FUN_004ec940(0,0x17,0,&local_8,0,1,0), then on success forwards it through FUN_004e1a80(1,&DAT_00871de0,...), matching the send pattern of FUN_00467010/FUN_004671d0 with message-type constant 0x17.
results.summary: Sends a small one-byte-payload network message tagged with type 0x17.

results.name: game_engine_reset_message_handler
results.evidence: Validates an incoming message via FUN_004ec590 (falls back to FUN_004ec670 on failure), and on success runs the same object-cleanup trio as FUN_00468260 (FUN_00467e60, FUN_00468010, FUN_00467f70) followed by the optional engine callback at DAT_006f1d20+0xac.
results.summary: Validates an incoming network message and, if valid, triggers the object-cleanup/reset pass and an engine callback.

results.name: ctf_flag_object_create
results.evidence: Builds a placement/location struct from an EAX-supplied Point3D-like triple, resolves a role/owner value (0 in certain multiplayer + tag-dependency cases, else 3) and calls the already-named object_new_with_datum_role_control to spawn it, then clears a flags bit and optionally calls FUN_004f50f0.
results.summary: Creates a new objective (flag) game object at a given location with a role/owner determined by the current multiplayer/tag state.

results.name: ctf_flag_object_respawn_for_team
results.evidence: If the per-team flag-exists table (DAT_006b0e88[team]) is non-zero, calls FUN_00468360 to spawn a fresh flag object and, on success, stores its handle into the per-team object-handle table DAT_006b0e90[team].
results.summary: Respawns a team's objective (flag) object if that team is configured to have one, recording the new object's handle.

results.name: ctf_flag_update_score_for_both_teams
results.evidence: Computes two team indices by toggling the low bit of unaff_EAX (x&0x80000001 and (x+1)&0x80000001, the same two-team wraparound idiom used throughout this cluster) and calls FUN_00460ba0 once for each, i.e. once per team.
results.summary: Invokes a per-team update/notify routine for both the current team and its opposing team.

results.name: ctf_flag_reset_team_return_credit
results.evidence: Zeroes the per-team defense/credit arrays DAT_006b0ea4 and DAT_006b0ea8 at the unit's team index (+0xb8), and if that team currently has a flag object (DAT_006b0e88[team] != 0) calls FUN_004666c0 (clear carrier fields) and sets/clears object flag bits at +0x22c/+0x10.
results.summary: Resets a team's flag-return credit tracking and, if a flag object exists for that team, clears its carrier state and updates its flag bits.

results.name: ctf_flag_attach_to_unit
results.evidence: Resolves the unit handle from a player index, and if that unit's object-type field (+4) is 0 calls FUN_0056dcd0(1); unconditionally calls FUN_0056dec0(handle,1) and then FUN_00468840 (reset team return credit).
results.summary: Attaches/updates a flag-carry state on a player's unit, then resets the associated team's flag-return credit.

results.name: ctf_flag_award_touch_medal
results.evidence: Increments a per-team touch counter (DAT_006b0e98[team]) and a per-player short field (players-array +200), optionally notifies via FUN_00466cb0(-1) when DAT_00719720==2, calls FUN_0046be40(1), then FUN_00460c10(param_1,0x21,0x23,0x22,param_1) -- the same helper used elsewhere in this file with medal/event-id-like constants.
results.summary: Increments a player's/team's flag-touch counters and fires an associated medal/event notification.

results.name: ctf_flag_position_within_radius
results.evidence: Treats DAT_006b0e88[in_EAX] as a float* (position) and, if non-null, computes squared 3D distance to a passed-in point (in_ECX) and compares it against param_1 squared, returning a boolean-ish packed result.
results.summary: Tests whether a given point lies within a given radius of a per-team position (interpreted here as the team's flag location).

results.name: ctf_flag_periodic_update_throttle
results.evidence: Compares a stored timestamp DAT_006b0eb4 against the current game time (DAT_006f1d6c+0xc); once it elapses, calls FUN_0046be40(1) and reschedules DAT_006b0eb4 to now + 0x78 (120 ticks / 4 seconds).
results.summary: Throttles a periodic flag-related update/notify call to at most once every four seconds.

results.name: ctf_flag_find_referencing_datum
results.evidence: Iterates every entry via data_iterator_next and, for valid ones, scans a 4-element handle array at object+0x2f8 for a match against unaff_EBX; both the match and no-match paths return 0xffffffff in the decompiled form, suggesting a hidden register carries the real result that Ghidra did not recover.
results.summary: Scans all datum entries' 4-slot handle arrays for a match against a given handle; the decompiled result is always -1, indicating an unmodeled output register.

results.name: ctf_engine_flag_tick
results.evidence: References the strings 'flag_blue'/'default'; toggles the active team between 0/1 via the (x+1)&0x80000001 idiom, counts down a return timer DAT_006b0eb0 against DAT_006f1d08, resets the DAT_006f18xx flag position/rotation fields and DAT_006b0eaX credit arrays, and calls chimera__kill_feed(0xffffffff,0x2d,...) (a flag-returned style event) when the flag auto-returns; also force-returns a flag left dropped for more than 0x1fe (~17s at 30 ticks/s) ticks, gated on the carrying unit's current weapon must_be_readied flag.
results.summary: Per-tick update of the CTF flag object: advances the auto-return countdown, resets flag state and cycles the active team when it expires, and force-returns a flag idle too long.

results.name: ctf_flag_unit_is_valid_carrier
results.evidence: Checks that the caller's per-team flag-handle table entry (DAT_006b0e90[team]) is valid, resolves the corresponding equipment/weapon-slot object via object_try_and_get, and that a further chained field (+0xc0 then +0x11c) is also valid, returning 1 only if the whole chain resolves.
results.summary: Checks whether a unit is currently a valid holder of its team's objective (flag) object by walking the object/equipment reference chain.

results.name: ctf_flag_carrier_tick
results.evidence: For a given (unit, team) pair in multiplayer (DAT_00719720==2), compares the unit's own team (+0xb8) against the passed team; when they match and the unit isn't already flagged as carrying (+0x22c bit 0x40), calls game_engine_is_inactive and, once inactive, resets per-team credit arrays, bumps a touch counter, and calls FUN_00460c10 with event ids; when they differ, sets the carrying flag and records touch/defense counters.
results.summary: Per-tick per-player handling of objective (flag) pickup/carry/drop bookkeeping and associated event notifications.

results.name: point3d_array_extract_xz_pairs
results.evidence: Copies from a stride-0xc (3-float, Point3D-sized) source array into a stride-8 (2-float) destination array, taking elements 0 and 2 of each triple (skipping the middle float) -- exactly the shape needed to feed 2D (x,z) points into the polygon2d_convex_hull_build call in its caller, FUN_0046a240.
results.summary: Extracts the X/Z components of an array of 3D points into a packed 2D point array, dropping the Y (vertical) component.

results.name: game_engine_pick_random_value_excluding
results.evidence: Advances a linear-congruential state (DAT_00719cd0 = DAT_00719cd0*0x19660d+0x3c6ef35f) and uses it to index a fixed-size candidate list (DAT_006b1070, length DAT_006b106c), returning the first candidate encountered that differs from the passed-in value.
results.summary: Picks a pseudo-random entry from a small fixed list that differs from a given value, using an inline LCG random-number generator.

results.name: game_engine_build_starting_location_boundary
results.evidence: Calls the already-named game_engine_find_valid_starting_locations to gather spawn points, runs FUN_0046a130 (extract 2D points) and polygon2d_convex_hull_build over them, then computes the resulting hull's axis-aligned bounding box and stores its center (DAT_006b1044/48/4c) and vertical range (DAT_006b105c/1060, expanded by 0.8/-0.1).
results.summary: Builds a 2D convex-hull boundary around a set of valid starting locations and computes its bounding-box center and vertical extent.

results.name: game_engine_render_starting_location_boundary_fence
results.evidence: Walks the convex-hull vertex list built by FUN_0046a240 (DAT_006b0f50 count, DAT_006b0f54.. positions), computes per-edge lengths and a normalized edge-plane normal (cross product against a vertically offset copy of the edge, offset by 0.8), and submits per-edge vertex/UV/normal data to FUN_0046b2f0.
results.summary: Generates and submits a fence-like quad mesh (with per-edge normals and UVs) along the starting-location boundary polygon, likely for a visual boundary effect.
